text:
The Community Nurse Supervisor
Community Nursing Centre
Newtown
11th February, 2018

Dear Sir/ Madam,

Re: Mr Ted Watson, aged 72

I am writing to refer Mr Watson who was admitted to our hospital on 10th May for rehabilitation following a surgical repair of a fractured right neck of femur.  He is due for discharge today and requires your continuous care and support.

During hospitalization, Mr Watson has made slow progress as a urinary tract infection developed resulting in a period of confusion and febrile. This has resolved with the treatment of Trimethoprim, Ural and Paracetamol. He is now self-managed his permanent indwelling catheter well. Moreover, his newly developed arterial leg ulcer in his right ankle has improved after being dressing regularly with Duoderm. As for his mobility, Mr Watson can only mobilise slowly with a pick-up frame, and requires maximal assistance for showering and dressing. 

Mr Watson lives alone on the ground floor, with a supportive daughter visiting frequently. His home modifications have been set readily for his self-care after discharge.  

Would you please continue to assist Mr Watson for his would dressing and personal hygiene? Please note that his urinary catheter needs to be changed every six week. 

Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any questions.

Yours sincerely,
RN
(191W)
